title: Espaces stratifiés et voisinages côniques (ou : déploiement des espaces stratifiés) : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting. I is a poset (in the surrounding notes, the poset indexing the strata of a stratified space X). A 'bande' (band) is a convex subset of I: if a ≤ i ≤ b with a, b in the subset, then i is in the subset. On the previous page Grothendieck introduces, for bands J and L:
- X_J^*, the union of the strata indexed by J;
- V_J, the tubular pro-neighbourhood of X_J^* in X, written as a colimit of the V_i and V_ij;
- V_J^L = V_J ∩ X_L^*, the trace of the J-tube on the L-part. This is the 'recollement' (gluing) datum between X_J^* and X_L^*.
He observes that V_J^L only depends on two smaller pieces:
- J_0 ⊂ J, the elements below some element of L (an ideal of J);
- L_0 ⊂ L, the elements above some element of J (a coideal of L).
This leads to the domination relation J ≺ L: every element of J lies below some element of L, and every element of L lies above some element of J.

This page is the order-theoretic lemma that clarifies ≺. For subsets J, L of I the following are equivalent:
(a) J and L are bands and J ≺ L;
(b) there is a band I' of I such that J is an ideal (down-closed) of I', L is a coideal (up-closed) of I', and every element of I' lies above some element of J and below some element of L.
Under these conditions I' is unique. It is the smallest band containing J ∪ L, namely
I' = {i ∈ I | there exist j ∈ J, l ∈ L with j ≤ i ≤ l}.

Proof (a ⇒ b).
- I' contains J ∪ L by the domination condition.
- I' is convex: if j1 ≤ i1 ≤ i ≤ i2 ≤ l2, then i lies in I'.
- Any convex set containing J ∪ L contains I', so I' is the smallest such band.
- J is an ideal of I': if i ∈ I' and i ≤ j ∈ J, pick j0 ∈ J with j0 ≤ i ≤ j; convexity of J gives i ∈ J.
- Dually, L is a coideal of I'.
- The betweenness property holds by definition of I'.

What the lemma serves. A dominated pair J ≺ L is the same thing as a convex subposet I' split into a 'bottom' ideal J and a 'top' coideal L. This is the indexing needed to view V_J^L as the deleted tubular neighbourhood (link-type object) of X_J^* inside the stratified space X_{I'}^*. It generalises the link V_i ∩ X_j of a pair of strata i < j. It is part of the combinatorial scaffolding for 'déploiement' (unfolding) of stratified spaces via pro-tubular neighbourhoods.
errors: The implication b ⇒ a is called trivial but not written out; it is indeed easy. J is convex in I because I' is convex and J is an ideal of I'; dually for L.

Uniqueness of I' is asserted but not proved in the text. It follows at once: any I' as in (b) is contained in the hull by the betweenness condition, and contains the hull because it is convex and contains J ∪ L.

The crossed-out condition 3° (l ≤ j with j ∈ J, l ∈ L implies j, l ∈ J ∩ L) is in fact a consequence of (b). From l ∈ I' and l ≤ j ∈ J, the ideal property gives l ∈ J; from j ∈ I' and j ≥ l ∈ L, the coideal property gives j ∈ L. So it was rightly deleted as redundant.

ideas.what: Bands (convex subsets) of the stratification poset and the domination relation J ≺ L.
ideas.modern_name: Convex subposets / intervals of a poset; ideal–coideal decomposition of a convex subset.

ideas.what: J ≺ L is equivalent to J and L being the ideal and coideal parts of their convex hull I', with I' unique and given by the 'between' formula.
ideas.modern_name: Convex hull in a poset; elementary lemma.

ideas.what: Using pairs of bands (J, L) to index the gluing data V_J^L = V_J ∩ X_L^* between the parts of a stratified space, i.e. generalised links indexed by convex subposets.
ideas.modern_name: Generalised homotopy links / links indexed by decompositions of subposets in poset-stratified spaces (exit-path, stratified homotopy theory).
ideas.usually_credited_to: Quinn and Hughes (homotopy links), Lurie (Higher Algebra, Appendix A), Ayala–Francis–Tanaka, Haine, Douteau, Waas (generalised links indexed by chains).
ideas.where_published: The Esquisse d'un programme mentions a theory of 'dévissage' of stratified structures and tubular neighbourhoods, but this band formalism does not appear there.

deep.surprise_reason: The page is a routine, correct order-theoretic lemma about convex subsets of a poset. Its only interest is as scaffolding for Grothendieck's unpublished theory of tubular pro-neighbourhoods of stratified spaces. That framework, links indexed by pairs of convex subposets, has close modern analogues in stratified homotopy theory, so it is not a missed result.
transcription_corrections: The formula label rendered '(bf)' is most likely the handwritten '(*)'; the marginal addition later refers to 'I' est donné par (*)'.
The marginal note 'i.e. J ≺ L' belongs to condition a) as a whole (1° and 2°), on the left margin.
'majorisé' on the previous page and 'majoré' here are the same notion.
